subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should this issue be narrowed to exposing a deletable `memory_recall` selector now, or folded into the broader memory lifecycle and conflict-resolution contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing UUIDs, accepting numeric recall indices, adding query fallback, or replacing/deprecating conflicting facts each creates different memory API and safety semantics.

options.title: Expose recall UUIDs first
options.body: Add model-visible UUIDs to `memory_recall` output so exact `memory_forget(memoryId=...)` can round-trip, while leaving replacement and tombstone semantics to the broader lifecycle issue.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle MVP
options.body: Keep this as a concrete symptom under the broader memory review/edit/forget/conflict-resolution tracker and wait for that product contract before changing tool output.

options.title: Design replacement semantics now
options.body: Use this issue to define automatic replace/deprecate behavior for conflicting facts, accepting a larger storage and UX design surface before implementation.

recommendation.title: Expose recall UUIDs first
recommendation.body: Add model-visible UUIDs to `memory_recall` output so exact `memory_forget(memoryId=...)` can round-trip, while leaving replacement and tombstone semantics to the broader lifecycle issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-lancedb commits and the partial UUID candidate-list fix make steipete the best available routing candidate for the product/API decision.
